slices.name: Bounded trim, repeat, Boolean, offset and seeded deformation kernels
changes: Arc-length trim with closed wrap/open clamp, accumulated versus simultaneous contours and retained nib source spans remapped under anisotropic transforms.
Repeater anchor/scale powers, signed offsets, fractional copies, opacity ramps and above/below order; undefined scale powers fail with diagnostic locations.

Clipper2 Boolean modes retain holes and empty operands, topmost subtraction, all-operand intersection and native XOR parity. Quantization is 1/1024 unit with 1024 total input vertices per polygon operation.
Signed open parallel offsets retain topology; closed offsets expand/contract with miter/round/bevel joins and bounded round work.
Round-corner fillets, vertex/control pucker-bloat, center-to-edge linear twist falloff with interior samples, pure seeded/time-based wiggle and per-original-cubic arc-length zigzag.
Zero operators retain geometry; invalid complexity/generated work fails explicitly. Native frame-wide budget/compiler wiring remains pending.

slices.name: Typed shape sampling and native paint compiler
changes: Sample only the native animated-field registry and static shape controls, keeping opaque metadata out of evaluated state. Bound/clamp numeric fields and reject nonfinite inputs. Reserve path sampling work before cloning vertex arrays.

Capture upstream geometry bindings, apply ordered path operators and paint bottom-to-top. Groups retain independent paint transforms/opacity; outer paints consume transformed geometry with their own stroke width.
Repeater clones geometry and paint references together, preserving painted-copy gradients versus compound coordinates and above/below order; fractional copy opacity is applied once.
Individual trim retains binding provenance even when repeater copies share declared IDs. Merge clears consumed sources to avoid double painting.
Conservative cubic/stroke bounds, collapsed/tiny transform handling and aggregate geometry/reference-copy budgets. Full native evaluator/backend integration follows.
